statements.statement: Historical satellite imagery shows a substantially larger persistent open-water feature in the verified forest-pond basin than recent imagery.
statements.verification: multi-year optical image review; corrected pond geometry; seasonal evidence build

statements.statement: Recent higher-resolution imagery shows little or no open-water footprint comparable with the older persistent pond feature.
statements.verification: Sentinel-2 image review plus historical spatial alignment

statements.statement: Working image-based loss estimate is approximately 25,000 m² (2.5 ha), near 100% of the historical open-water footprint.
statements.limitations: Not final until corrected common-grid spectral endpoint measurement, manually verified pond polygon and uncertainty bounds are complete. Some older scenes visually suggest a larger maximum footprint.

statements.statement: Long-term or seasonal drought/precipitation deficit may contribute to water loss.
Drainage, channel connectivity, blocked/altered inflows or outflows, or water-routing/retention changes may contribute.
statements.verification_required: authoritative drainage/hydrology maps, field inspection, water-level/flow data and documented interventions

statements.statement: Groundwater change may contribute to the observed pond state transition.

If corrected measurements confirm near-total disappearance of a previously persistent hectare-scale pond, TerraWater should flag this location as a high-priority environmental monitoring anomaly requiring investigation.
statements.note: An anomaly flag does not establish cause, fault or a required physical intervention.
